item: A Stop through a loopback HTTP proxy is read as the Stop, a URL's credentials stay out of the failure sentence, and the inert DOTALL goes (R620)
summary: R620, three items in one PR. (a) A Stop through a LOOPBACK HTTP proxy (Privoxy chained to Tor) to an https target: the socket guard refuses the real destination in _guarded_tunnel, which urllib3 calls after _new_conn returned, so the fetcher wrote "request error for <url>: ('Connection aborted.', AirplaneModeError(\"airplane mode is engaged: refusing a network connection to '<host>'. ...\"))" (measured through the real guard, a loopback proxy, requests 2.34, urllib3 2.7.0 and 2.8.0; single quotes when the host holds one; the proxy receives no CONNECT byte). Before, no alternative of fetch_verdict._OFFLINE_RE read it and it was classified connect, a false 'not offline' that only the R320 switch read caught while the switch was still engaged; now a fourth alternative spells urllib3's construction from its first word with no gap. A host cannot write it: urllib3 writes 'Connection aborted.' once (connectionpool.py, for an OSError or an HTTPException; requests never), the tuple's second item is that exception's repr, and every such class on the fetch path opens its repr with its own name (BaseException's repr, or one of four overrides that do the same), so a host's words sit inside the quotes after a class name it cannot choose (BadStatusLine for a status line, OSError under ProxyError for a proxy's refused CONNECT); one class is named AirplaneModeError and its one writer opens with the guard's words. This narrows R320 for that one shape (it reads the whole construction, it does not widen), and the switch read stays for every other shape: the tests that pinned the shape as a non-match now pin it as a match, and the switch-clear direction uses a host's reset in the same wrapping. (b) failure_url wrote a URL's userinfo into the failure sentence (https://alice:hunter2@host/x, stored, served and shown); now the authority's userinfo and its @ are written ***@ (fixed length, the user name too, no whitespace and none of :/?#[]@, so host/port/path parse the same and the token stays one \S+), the span read wider than urlsplit and urllib3 (dropped tab/CR/LF skipped, leading whitespace skipped, any scheme before the first colon, authority to the first / ? # with the backslash, the last @), an @ in a path, query or fragment untouched, whitespace still percent-encoded, and it never raises (an unreadable input is written <url-withheld>). No consumer of 'request error for' parses the URL back out. (c) The inert re.DOTALL is dropped (no '.' stood outside a class or an escape); the flags pin says re.IGNORECASE. Tests: tests/test_refusal_r620.py (80 cases: the real shape through a loopback proxy for four hosts with the R616 reader shown not to read it; EthicalFetcher.fetch against a user:pass@ URL directly and through the proxy, offline and credential-free; live proxies writing the guard's words as status line or 403 reason; eleven forged shapes from real exception objects; source pins on urllib3 and on the one writer; a walk of every exception class on the fetch path and its repr; 22 credential forms; both parsers reading the same host, port and path after the mask; ten non-credential @; five unreadable inputs; 4000 seeded fuzz inputs; DOTALL shown inert), plus tests/test_kill_switch_refusal_constant.py, tests/test_csv_feeds_offline.py and tests/test_stop_is_not_an_outcome.py updated; green on urllib3 2.7.0 and 2.8.0. Sixteen mutants killed by named tests (alternative removed, four gaps, class name as \w+, mask removed, mask over the whole netloc, try/except removed, first @, dropped characters kept, authority ending at / only, leading whitespace kept, scheme prefix unchecked, DOTALL back, the base's behaviour); none survived. Not changed: the other FetchFailed sentences (HTTP <status> for <url>, robots.txt disallows <url>, the size, content-type, redirect and malformed-URL sentences) still write the raw URL. Release-notes line: When collection is stopped while it runs through a local proxy such as Privoxy, the app now reports those sources as offline instead of as connection failures, and a web address that carries a user name and password no longer shows them in fetch error messages.
